term: Religious Land Use and Institutionalized Persons Act (RLUIPA)
definition: A federal law passed in 2000 that prohibits state and local governments from using zoning and landmarking laws to substantially burden religious exercise unless the government can prove a compelling interest pursued in the least restrictive way. It was enacted after the Supreme Court limited other religious liberty protections.
examples: Grand invokes RLUIPA to challenge University Heights' ordinance preventing him from hosting prayer gatherings in his home.
